ready.title: hive: show test_writer the existing return contract and callers of
ready.body:
Cause: hive/test_grounding.py public_surface shows only bare signatures ('bodies not shown'). In run pilot-acb696cd8c11-1791023282 the test writer never saw that scraper.fetch_upload_date returns (date_str, time_str) or that scraper.py:330 unpacks a tuple. It asserted a bare ISO string or None, so all 4 acceptance tests were unsatisfiable without breaking callers. Nothing merged after 17 worker steps.

Change: add test_grounding.existing_contract(root, files_edit, interface). For each interface symbol defined in a files_edit module, it emits the first docstring paragraph, the unparsed return expressions (at most 5), and at most 3 repo call sites that consume the result (text search for '<name>(' outside tests). The output is capped at 2000 chars. test_writer.test_writer appends the block to the brief under the header 'EXISTING CONTRACT -- keep this return shape unless the TASK text changes it'. The prompt line 'you have NOT been shown any implementation' is relaxed to match.

Regression test (written first, from this spec): tests/test_test_grounding_contract.py builds a tmp repo with mod.py containing 'def f(x):\n    """Returns (a, b)."""\n    return a, b' and caller.py containing 'p, q = mod.f(1)'. It asserts that existing_contract includes 'Returns (a, b).', 'return (a, b)' and 'p, q = mod.f(1)', respects the cap, and returns '' for an interface that does not exist yet. A second test asserts that build_test_brief includes the EXISTING CONTRACT header when the helper returns text. Run ./run-tests.sh in full.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-acb696cd8c11-1791023282 (task acb696cd8c11: marketwatch: fetch_upload_date reads 1.5 MB and parses nothing).
Root cause: The test writer wrote an acceptance contract that contradicts the existing function, so no worker could pass it without breaking the caller. Hive's PUBLIC SURFACE grounding (hive/test_grounding.py public_surface, which calls public_signatures) gives the test writer only `def fetch_upload_date(video_id)`. Its header says "bodies not shown". The docstring "Returns (date_str, time_str)" and the tuple return were never shown, and neither was the caller at scraper.py:330, which unpacks `fetched_ud, fetched_time = fetch_upload_date(...)`. The test writer (cohere/north-mini-code) therefore invented a shape. Its tests assert `result == date_iso` (a bare ISO string), `result is None` when no date is found, and `mock_resp.close.assert_called_once()`. They also mock `iter_content` to yield bytes. The worker kept the real tuple API and decoded the chunks with `decode_unicode=True`. All 4 new tests fail against the final commit 7869262 (`assert ('', '') == '2023-07-01T00:00:00Z'`, plus stderr "Date fetch error ... object of type 'Mock' has no len()"). Worker iterations 2 and 3 produced 17 worker steps and 2 commits on cohere without ever going green. The integrator merged nothing, and the gate reported "0 files changed · 0 tests selected". The run spent 680 s and 186k input tokens on a contract that could not be met. A secondary defect also cost tokens: the worker never added the `"publishDate":"ISO"` pattern the spec names. That is a model-quality miss, but it would not have produced a merge on its own. Rate limits (22 failover hops) slowed the run but did not cause the failure, because every role eventually got an ok call.
Optimizations:
- [prompt_context] For each symbol named in the task Interface that already exists in a files_edit module, show the test writer the docstring and the return expressions (ast Return nodes, unparsed, capped at about 5 lines). Also show up to 3 caller lines from the repo that use its result, for example 'fetched_ud, fetched_time = fetch_upload_date(...)'. Label the block 'EXISTING CONTRACT -- keep this return shape unless the TASK text changes it'. (where: hive/test_grounding.py public_surface (new helper existing_contract(root, files, interface)), wired in hive/nodes/test_writer.py test_writer / build_test_brief) -> Tests for edits to existing functions assert the real return shape, so the worker can satisfy them without breaking callers. This removes the unsatisfiable-contract class that burned 17 worker steps and 180k tokens in this run.
- [smaller_units] Add a contract sanity check after the test writer runs. For an edit task, run the new tests against the unmodified base. If a failure is a shape or type mismatch on an existing interface (for example a tuple compared to a str, or an expected None where the base returns a tuple), regenerate the tests once with the failure shown. Otherwise fail fast before any worker steps. (where: hive/nodes/test_writer.py test_writer (post-write validation step)) -> Catches contradictory contracts in about 2 seconds of pytest instead of 2 worker iterations of roughly 8 minutes.
- [model_per_role] Move the test_writer list head from cohere/north-mini-code:free (50.1 s for one call in this run) to codestral-2508, which has 20 calls, 100% ok and a 6.3 s p50 in build-free history. Consider dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free ahead of cohere for the worker (97.4% ok and 0% rate-limited, against cohere's 93.4% ok and 5.7% rate-limited). (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] test_writer and worker lists) -> Faster and more reliable test writing, and fewer rate-limit failover hops on the worker (cohere caused 2 of the run's rate-limited worker calls and many of the 22 rate_limit hops). [needs captain review]
- [rate_limit_scheduling] When a 429 body carries 'Soonest reset ~Ns' with N at or under 90, sleep N seconds and retry the same rung instead of hopping. Record the wait in ratewait_s, which was 0.0 in this run despite 22 rate_limit hops. (where: hive failover wrapper around model calls (hive/profiles.py ordered failover)) -> Fewer failover hops onto weaker rungs, and accurate rate-wait metrics.
- [caching] Cache the PUBLIC SURFACE and existing-contract block per (repo, base sha, files) so retries and replans reuse it. (where: hive/test_grounding.py public_surface) -> Saves the os.walk and ast parse on each test-writer retry. This is a minor latency win.

ready.title: hive: Run shell-metachar acceptance tests through bash -c
ready.body:
hive/testing.py command_for() shlex-splits any acceptance entry containing a space and runs it with no shell. A planner pipeline such as "grep -A 8 'X' docs/TOOLS.md | grep -E '(a|b)'" then hands '|' to grep as a filename and fails every time (run pilot-675303caa07c-1791438640). Change: if the entry contains any of |, &&, ||, ;, >, <, $(, or a backtick, return TestCommand(argv=['bash','-c',entry], kind='shell'). Leave other space-containing entries on the shlex path. Regression tests in tests/test_testing.py: (1) command_for('hive', "grep -c x f | grep -E '(a|b)'").argv == ['bash','-c', <entry>]. (2) A plain 'grep -q x docs/TOOLS.md' still shlex-splits. (3) Executing the returned argv for a pipeline against a tmp file containing a matching line exits 0. Run ./run-tests.sh green before PR.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-675303caa07c-1791438640 (task 675303caa07c: hive: add hive chain output example to TOOLS.md).
Root cause: The worker's first real commit (9942416f, iter 2) was correct, but the acceptance test could never pass under hive's test runner. The planner wrote the acceptance test as a shell pipeline: "grep -A 8 'Shared chain availability and call capture' docs/TOOLS.md | grep -E '(MEMBER|benched|BENCHED|bench)'". hive/testing.py command_for() handles any entry containing a space with TestCommand(argv=shlex.split(entry), kind="shell"), and that argv runs with no shell. The '|' and the second grep therefore became extra filename arguments for the first grep, which exits 2 with "grep: |: No such file or directory". Reproducing that argv against the run's worktree gives exit 2 with that exact stderr. The same command run through bash on the same worktree exits 0. The adjudicator blamed the test twice (iters 2 and 3), but no path existed to repair a contract test. Iter 4 then wrongly blamed the module. The worker used 78 steps and 1.74M input tokens on a docs-only change, nothing merged, and the gate reported 0 files changed. The free models and the chain were not the cause: all 3 planner calls, 3 of 5 reviewer calls and 74 of 83 worker calls returned ok, and the 10 failover hops each recovered.
Optimizations:
- [other] When an acceptance entry contains shell metacharacters (|, &&, ||, ;, >, <, $(, backtick), return TestCommand(argv=['bash','-c',entry], kind='shell') instead of shlex.split(entry). Plain commands keep the shlex path. (where: hive/testing.py command_for()) -> Planner-written pipeline acceptance tests run as written. This run's iter-2 commit would have passed and landed after about 30 worker steps instead of failing after 78.
- [other] When adjudication returns side=test and the failure output shows a harness error (No such file or directory naming a shell token, command not found), stop the worker loop. Route the run to one replan of that task's acceptance_tests instead of more worker iterations. (where: hive/nodes/reviewer.py adjudicate() and the route after it in hive/graphs/build.py) -> A broken contract test costs one planner call, not two more full worker iterations (39 steps, about 900k input tokens in this run).
- [prompt_context] For docs-only tasks (every scoped file is .md), tell the planner to write a single-command acceptance test such as `grep -q '<literal>' docs/X.md` with no pipes and no -A windows. Reject plans whose acceptance test is a pipeline in Plan validation. (where: hive/prompts/planner.md and hive/contracts.py Plan validation (the acceptance_tests loop)) -> Removes the fragile pipeline-plus-window test class at plan time, before any worker tokens are spent.
- [smaller_units] Cap worker steps per iteration for tasks whose scope is docs-only, for example 8 steps, and end the iteration as soon as the acceptance test passes after a commit. (where: hive/tool_loop.py worker loop step budget) -> A 13-line docs edit cannot burn 30 steps in one iteration. Input tokens per docs task fall by about 70%.
- [caching] Cache acceptance-test results keyed by (command, worktree HEAD sha) so unchanged HEADs are not re-run, and feed the cached failure to the adjudicator once instead of per step. (where: hive/tool_loop.py acceptance-test run path (around the ctx.task.acceptance_tests loop)) -> Fewer redundant test runs and shorter repeated failure context in worker prompts.

ready.title: hive: Retry transient upstream errors inside the free failover list
ready.body:
In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, a member that fails with a transient upstream error (502/503 upstream_failed, 'stream ended unexpectedly', connection reset) sets limited_only=False. The loop then breaks without a wait or retry. Run pilot-0c6eacb8f3c8-1791441876 died this way: kilo nemotron returned one 502 truncation 7 s after succeeding, and the other 3 planner members were benched or on cooldown. Change: add rate_limits.is_transient_upstream(error). In _invoke_chain, retry such a member once after rate_limits.sleep(TRANSIENT_RETRY_S, default 5) before handing over. A pass whose failures are all transient or rate-limit keeps limited_only true so the existing ratewait loop runs. Log the retry as a failover row with finish_reason failover:transient. Regression tests in tests/test_models_chain.py (or the existing chain test file): (1) members [a, b, c], with b and c benched and a returning a 502 'stream ended unexpectedly' then ok, gives ok with 2 calls to a. (2) A 401 auth error on a is still not retried. (3) is_transient_upstream is true for the run's exact 502 text and false for a 429. Run ./run-tests.sh green before the PR.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-0c6eacb8f3c8-1791441876 (task 0c6eacb8f3c8: 0c6eacb8f3c8).
Root cause: Two stacked causes. (1) The task spec named a regression-test file that does not exist. The first plan (kilo nemotron-3-ultra, ok after about 9 minutes of rate waits) copied the spec and put tests/test_testing.py in files_edit. grounding_problems rejected it with "files_edit 'tests/test_testing.py' does not exist in the repo (did you mean hive/testing.py, tests/test_testing_commands.py?)". I reproduced this offline from the raw plan file. Nothing else was wrong with the plan, so it went to planner retry 1. (2) Retry 1 ran the planner failover list when only one member could be called. cloudflare qwen3.8-27b was benched until 2026-10-09, requesty nemotron was benched until 06:58:02, and groq qwen3.8-27b was on cooldown. groq also cannot take this prompt at all: its input cap is 7000 tokens per minute and the planner prompt is about 7305 tokens. The one callable member, kilo nemotron, which had succeeded 7 s earlier, returned a transient 502 "stream ended unexpectedly" in 1.09 s. In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, that non-rate-limit error sets limited_only=False, so the loop breaks with no wait and no second try. A chain member also never gets a same-model retry, because invoke_with_ledger breaks when _chain is set and the result is not truncated. _planner then raises ModelError on the failed retry. The run died from one transient upstream blip while the only usable model was healthy. The free models were not otherwise at fault: the only real planner call returned ok.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] Treat a transient upstream error (502/503 with upstream_failed, or 'stream ended unexpectedly' or a connection reset) as retryable. Retry that member once after a short backoff (about 5 s) before handing over to the next one. When a pass ends with only transient errors plus benched or cooldown members, keep limited_only true so the existing wait-and-retry loop runs instead of breaking. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (limited_only decision and per-member call), with a classifier helper is_transient_upstream() in hive/rate_limits.py) -> A one-off gateway truncation on the only healthy member no longer kills the run. This run's retry 1 would have gone to the same nemotron that answered 7 s earlier and continued to build.
- [smaller_units] In plan repair, when a files_edit path under tests/ does not exist but its parent directory does, move it to files_create and record a repair note instead of raising a grounding problem. (where: hive/contracts.py Plan.repair (and grounding_problems in hive/nodes/planner.py so it stops flagging the moved entry)) -> Plans that name a new test file in files_edit pass without a planner retry. This removes the second planner call that this run died on.
- [prompt_context] Tell the failure-analysis author to name only test files that exist in the repo (it has Glob) or to say 'new file' explicitly in the task body. (where: hive/failure_analysis.py analysis prompt text) -> Follow-up tasks filed from analyses no longer seed plans with nonexistent files_edit paths.
- [rate_limit_scheduling] Record a member's hard per-request input cap when a 413 'Request too large ... ITPM Limit N' comes back. Skip that member when the estimated prompt tokens exceed N, without spending a call or a wait pass on it. (where: hive/member_bench.py (store cap from 413) and hive/models.py _invoke_chain member loop) -> No wasted calls or rate waits on groq qwen3.8-27b for planner prompts above 7000 tokens, so the list stops counting a member that can never serve.
- [model_per_role] The planner list has one effective member: cloudflare is daily-benched, groq's input cap is below the prompt size, and requesty shares the same nemotron and is often rate limited. Replace the groq qwen3.8-27b planner rung with a member that has a measured 100% planner or reviewer history and a larger input cap, for example gemini-3.7-flash via a free platform or glm-4.5-flash. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] planner list) -> At least two independent, callable planner members, which cuts the 353 s of rate waits and single-point failures in the plan phase. [needs captain review]

ready.title: hive: Treat 413 context_length_exceeded as non-rate-limit in failover
ready.body:
Run pilot-45b4c947cc03-1791441967 failed because groq qwen3.8-27b returned 413 context_length_exceeded. The aggregator's body says 'All models exhausted ... wait for rate limits to reset'. rate_limits.is_rate_limited() matches 'rate limit', and notify.classify_model_error() returns 'quota' on 'exhausted'. As a result, _invoke_chain kept limited_only=True, put groq on a 10-minute cooldown, and spent 311 s in ratewait for a member that can never fit the prompt.

Change:
1. hive/notify.py classify_model_error: return a new kind 'too_large' when the error contains '413', 'context_length_exceeded' or 'prompt too large'. Check this before the quota and rate hints.
2. hive/rate_limits.py is_rate_limited: return False when classify_model_error gives 'too_large'.
3. hive/models.py _invoke_chain: a 'too_large' result sets limited_only=False and never calls COOLDOWNS.note or member_bench.bench_for. Its failover row carries finish_reason 'failover:too_large'.

Regression test (tests/test_models_chain_too_large.py, written first from this spec):
(a) is_rate_limited() is False on the verbatim 413 string from this run, quoted in the test.
(b) In _invoke_chain with members [A, B], where A is benched by a fake chain_state and B's invoke_with_ledger returns that 413 error, the call returns a failed CallResult with no ratewait ledger row, rate_limits.sleep is never called, and COOLDOWNS.until(B) == 0.
(c) A real 429 still produces a ratewait. Run ./run-tests.sh in full.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-45b4c947cc03-1791441967 (task 45b4c947cc03: 45b4c947cc03).
Root cause: Three faults stacked, and the planner never got a usable answer. (1) At launch, 3 of the 4 planner members were benched by the chain: cloudflare qwen3.8-27b until 2026-10-09T00:00 (its daily quota), kilo nemotron-ultra until 06:55:55 and requesty nemotron-ultra until 06:47:57. That left groq qwen3.8-27b as the only member hive could call. (2) Groq rejected the planner prompt with 413 context_length_exceeded, which means the prompt will never fit that member. The aggregator's 413 body happens to contain "All models exhausted ... wait for rate limits to reset". hive.rate_limits.is_rate_limited() matches the substring "rate limit", and notify.classify_model_error() returns "quota" because of "exhausted". I ran both on the verbatim error and they returned True and "quota". So _invoke_chain kept limited_only=True and set a 10-minute cooldown on groq ("rate limited until 06:56:46"). It then spent 311 s in three ratewait passes waiting for a member that can never take this prompt. (3) After the waits, the call to kilo nemotron-ultra hit hive's 120 s CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S, and requesty nemotron-ultra returned an upstream 502. That exhausted the list at 06:55. The planner list holds only 2 distinct models across 4 rungs. One of them, qwen3.8-27b, cannot fit the prompt on groq, so the run effectively depended on a single model, nemotron-ultra, that was benched or failing on both providers.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] Classify 413 / context_length_exceeded / 'prompt too large' as a permanent 'too_large' failure before any rate-limit match. In is_rate_limited(), return False when the error carries 413 or context_length_exceeded. In _invoke_chain, treat 'too_large' as limited_only=False with no COOLDOWNS.note or bench, and log the failover row as failover:too_large. This stops ratewait from sleeping for a member that can never fit the prompt. (where: hive/rate_limits.py is_rate_limited; hive/notify.py classify_model_error (add a context_length hint ahead of the _QUOTA_HINTS check); hive/models.py _invoke_chain) -> Cuts the 311 s of wasted ratewait in this run. A 413 hands over immediately, so the wait budget goes to members that are genuinely rate-limited and the planner timeline stays inside budget.
- [prompt_context] Before calling a planner member, estimate prompt tokens with _estimate_tokens. If the estimate exceeds the member's known context window (learned from a prior 413 on that member and cached per run), skip that member or send a trimmed planner prompt that keeps the task spec and drops the digest and rules tail. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (pre-call size check); hive/nodes/planner.py (trimmed-prompt builder)) -> Groq qwen3.8-27b, the planner member with 100% success and a 1.8 s p50, stays usable on long task specs like this two-defect one instead of 413ing.
- [model_per_role] Give the planner list a third distinct model with measured history, for example glm-4.7-flash or gemini-3.7-flash, which are 100% ok in the reviewer role, as long as distinct_roles still holds. Today the 4 rungs cover only 2 models, so one model being benched on both providers empties the list. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free].planner) -> Removes the single point of failure that sank this run: nemotron-ultra benched or 502ing on both kilo and requesty while qwen could not fit the prompt. [needs captain review]
- [rate_limit_scheduling] Give the planner role a per-role stall timeout of about 3x its measured p50 (nemotron-ultra planner p50 54.9 s, so 180 s) instead of the global 120 s CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (_ChainMember timeout_s), driven by member_bench latency history) -> The kilo nemotron-ultra call that timed out at 121 s would likely have completed. The planner's slow but reliable model stops being cut off.
- [caching] Have the launch step read chain_state for every planner member before starting. If every member is benched past the wait budget, for example a daily-quota bench until 00:00, defer the run with a scheduled retry at the soonest unbench instead of launching and failing. (where: hive/graphs/build_free.py launch path / hive/chain_state.py) -> Avoids spending about 9 minutes and a failed-run Opus analysis on a run whose planner list was already dead at launch.

ready.title: hive: Treat missing acceptance runner binary as infra_failed
ready.body:
Root cause (run pilot-b7604a01eff1-1791443922): `cargo check -p buzz-pubsub` raised FileNotFoundError because hive-dev.service PATH lacks ~/.cargo/bin. hive/nodes/worker.py run_checks wrote 'Test <entry> exception: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'cargo''. project_env.RUNNER_MISSING_PATTERNS did not match it, so a correct diff looped through 4 fix iterations and 3 adjudications and never merged.

Change:
1. hive/nodes/worker.py run_checks acceptance loop: catch FileNotFoundError (and OSError errno ENOENT) separately from other exceptions. Write 'Test <entry> failed: runner missing: <argv0> not found on PATH' and log the acceptance row with rc=127.
2. hive/project_env.py RUNNER_MISSING_PATTERNS: add 'runner missing:' and the exec-failure form "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '" so is_runner_missing() is True for any missing argv[0].
3. Keep every existing pattern. Surgical diff, do not rewrite either file.

Regression tests (write first, from this spec):
- tests/test_project_env.py: is_runner_missing("Test cargo check -p x exception: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'cargo'") is True, and is_runner_missing('AssertionError: 1 != 2') stays False.
- tests/test_worker_checks.py: run run_checks with a fake worktree whose task has acceptance_tests=['hive-no-such-binary-xyz check'] and assert the tail contains 'runner missing'. Run the tool worker status path with that tail and assert status == 'infra_failed'.

Separate follow-up, not this task: add %h/.cargo/bin to hive-dev.service PATH and fix the Windows CARGO_TARGET_DIR in [projects.buzz.tests].

Gate: ./run-tests.sh fully green.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-b7604a01eff1-1791443922 (task b7604a01eff1: Relay proof: clarify subscriber reconnect backoff doc comments in buzz-pubsub).
Root cause: The worker's diff was correct on the first try. It was committed as 0d3bdfcdc and matched the spec byte for byte. The run still failed because the only acceptance test, `cargo check -p buzz-pubsub`, could not start. The hive-dev.service unit on homelab sets PATH=%h/bin:%h/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, and cargo lives in ~/.cargo/bin, outside that PATH. wt.run raised FileNotFoundError, and hive/nodes/worker.py:700 recorded it as "Test cargo check -p buzz-pubsub exception: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'cargo'". project_env.RUNNER_MISSING_PATTERNS only matches "No such file or directory: 'python" and "command not found", so is_runner_missing returned False. The worker therefore marked the result "failed" instead of "infra_failed". That sent a correct doc-comment change through 4 fix iterations (32 worker steps, 243k input tokens, 1214 s). The reviewer adjudicated 3 times, and every verdict said the test environment was at fault and the module was correct. The fix brief told the worker to edit a test that does not exist, so nothing converged and nothing merged. A second, latent bug in the same path: policy.toml [projects.buzz.tests] sets CARGO_TARGET_DIR='E:\.rust-cache\hive' for crates/**/*.rs. That is a Windows path, and it is wrong on homelab. Free-model quality and rate limits were not the cause: every model call that mattered succeeded.
Optimizations:
- [other] Classify a missing acceptance-runner binary as infra. In the acceptance loop's `except Exception` branch, catch FileNotFoundError (or OSError with errno ENOENT) and write a tail line that contains a RUNNER_MISSING_PATTERNS marker, for example 'runner missing: <argv0> not found on PATH'. Also add the generic "No such file or directory: '" exec-failure form to RUNNER_MISSING_PATTERNS so tool_worker/worker/file_worker/acp_worker set status=infra_failed. The run then stops after one iteration instead of looping fix rounds and adjudications on correct code. (where: hive/nodes/worker.py run_checks acceptance loop (line ~700) and hive/project_env.py RUNNER_MISSING_PATTERNS) -> A run with a missing toolchain fails fast as infra_failed in under 2 minutes instead of ~20 minutes and 240k tokens. The captain sees the real cause instead of 'nothing merged'.
- [other] Put the Rust toolchain on the hive-dev runner's PATH: append %h/.cargo/bin to Environment=PATH in hive-dev.service. Also correct [projects.buzz.tests] CARGO_TARGET_DIR so homelab does not get the Windows 'E:\.rust-cache\hive' path. Use a per-host value or drop the env override on non-Windows hosts. (where: ~/.config/systemd/user/hive-dev.service (chezmoi-managed unit) and hive/policy.toml [projects.buzz.tests]; host resolution in hive/testing.py command_for) -> cargo check/test acceptance entries for Buzz crates actually run on homelab, so this doc-only task lands on the first iteration.
- [prompt_context] Cap fix iterations when every adjudication verdict is side=test and no test file exists in the plan. Fold an all-environment adjudication into an immediate infra_failed stop rather than a fix brief that tells the worker to edit a nonexistent test. (where: hive/nodes/reviewer.py _adjudication_fix_brief / adjudicate caller) -> Removes iterations 2-4 (about 190k worker input tokens) whenever the adjudicator has already exonerated the module.
- [smaller_units] For doc-comment-only or comment-only diffs (every changed hunk touches only comment lines), skip the worker's iterative fix loop after the first passing compile-or-unrunnable check and hand the change straight to the integrator gate. (where: hive/nodes/tool_worker.py status decision, with a helper in hive/gate_suite.py) -> Trivial doc tasks finish in one worker iteration (~2 minutes) regardless of acceptance-runner availability.
- [prompt_context] Trim the per-step worker context. Worker agnes-2.5-flash averaged ~7.5k tokens in per call for a 2-line edit, and later tool steps reached 54k-token raw files. Cap repeated test_output_tail and transcript replay per step. (where: hive/nodes/tool_worker.py prompt/transcript assembly) -> Lower token use per step and fewer rate-limit hops (50 failover hops in this run).

ready.title: hive: Failover list waits for benched members after a timeout
ready.body:
In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, one member timing out sets limited_only=False. The loop then breaks without waiting, even when other members were skipped only because they were benched or on cooldown and reset within WAIT_BUDGET_S. Run pilot-11b7060b4962-1791445201 failed this way: kilo nemotron timed out, and requesty nemotron's bench ended 8 minutes later. Change: track the members skipped for bench or cooldown during a pass. If no member succeeded and any were skipped, call rate_limits.wait_seconds(soonest, ...), bounded by WAIT_BUDGET_S and wait_until. Log the ratewait row and re-run a pass over only the skipped members. Never re-call a member that timed out or errored in this invocation. Regression test, written first, in tests/: a list [A, B] where A times out (fake invoke_with_ledger) and B is benched until now+30s with rate_limits.sleep patched. Assert one ratewait row, B called once after the wait, A called exactly once, result ok. A second case: B benched past the budget means no wait and the call fails with 'failover list exhausted'.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-11b7060b4962-1791445201 (task 11b7060b4962: 11b7060b4962).
Root cause: The planner list had only one callable member when the run reached it, and the failover loop gave up instead of waiting for a member that would come back. At launch, 3 of the 4 planner members were unavailable. cloudflare qwen3.8-27b was benched until 2026-10-09T00:00Z. requesty nemotron-ultra was benched until 07:50:52Z. groq qwen3.8-27b was rate limited until 08:15:27Z. The one member hive actually called, kilo nemotron-ultra:free, hit the 120 s CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S and returned "Request timed out." In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, a timeout is not a rate limit, so it sets limited_only = False. The `if not limited_only: break` then ends the loop and skips the rate-wait path, even though requesty nemotron-ultra was due back about 8 minutes after the 07:43Z failure. That is well inside the 600 s WAIT_BUDGET_S. That member has a 100% planner record (9/9 ok). The run failed with ratewait_s = 0 and spent no tokens. Two smaller factors made it worse. The list holds only two distinct models, each on two platforms, so a chain bench or cooldown on one model removes half the list. The member tried first is also the slowest planner model (p50 54.9 s), and qwen3.8-27b answers in 1.8 s.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] When a pass ends with no success, wait if any member was skipped as benched or on cooldown. The wait lasts until the soonest reset, within WAIT_BUDGET_S and wait_until. Only those skipped members are retried. A member that timed out or errored in this call is not retried. Track this with a `waitable` flag set only on the skip path, so a timeout no longer cancels the wait. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (the limited_only/break logic and the retry pass)) -> This run would have waited about 8 minutes for requesty nemotron-ultra, which has a 100% planner record, and then planned. Planner failures caused by mixed bench and timeout states turn into short waits.
- [model_per_role] Reorder the planner list so groq qwen3.8-27b (p50 1.8 s) is tried before the 55 s nemotron-ultra members. Add a third distinct free planner model so that benching one model cannot remove half the list. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] planner) -> The first planner attempt finishes in seconds most of the time. The list survives a whole model family being benched. [needs captain review]
- [prompt_context] Use a longer stall timeout for planner-tier members, since nemotron-ultra p50 is 54.9 s. Alternatively, record and trim the planner prompt size before the call, so a slow model is not cut off at 120 s mid-generation. (where: hive/models.py CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S / _ChainMember timeout_s chosen per tier in _invoke_chain) -> Fewer false timeouts on slow but reliable planner models.
- [rate_limit_scheduling] Before the planner starts, check whether every planner member is benched or on cooldown. If so, put the run on the queue until the soonest reset instead of spending the run on a 120 s timeout. (where: hive/graphs/build_free.py launch path, using chain_state.STATE.benched_until and rate_limits.COOLDOWNS.until) -> Runs start when the planner list is available, not into a list that is mostly benched.

ready.outcome: A free run whose only callable member times out waits for a benched member's reset within budget, then succeeds.

ready.title: hive: Failover list waits for near benches after a member timeout
ready.body:
Change hive/models.py _invoke_failover_list. Today any non-rate-limit failure such as a timeout sets limited_only=False, and the loop breaks without waiting. It should wait whenever a pass had at least one member skipped for a chain bench or a local cooldown and rate_limits.wait_seconds(soonest, ...) returns > 0. Members that timed out, errored, came back empty or stayed truncated during this call go into a per-call failed_hard set. They are skipped on later passes, so they are never re-called. Break when no member is both outside failed_hard and pending a reset within budget or deadline. Keep the ratewait ledger row and the existing exhausted-list error text. Regression test first, in tests/: a 3-member list where member A times out, member B is benched by chain_state until now+30 s, and member C is on cooldown past the budget. Use fake clock and sleep. Assert one ratewait row, then B is called and returns ok. Assert A is called exactly once. Add a second test: A times out and B and C are benched beyond WAIT_BUDGET_S. Assert the call fails with no wait. Run ./run-tests.sh fully green.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-5cf5636064cc-1791445211 (task 5cf5636064cc: 5cf5636064cc).
Root cause: The planner never got a usable model, and hive gave up while a planner model was due back within its own wait budget. The first planner member (kilo nemotron-3-ultra:free) spent the whole 120 s CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S and timed out. The other three were skipped without a request. Cloudflare qwen3.8-27b was benched until 2026-10-09 by its daily quota. Requesty nemotron-3-ultra was benched until 07:50:52, about 8 minutes after the 07:43:00 hop. Groq qwen3.8-27b was cooling down until 08:15:27. In hive/models.py _invoke_failover_list, any non-rate-limit failure such as a timeout sets limited_only=False. The loop then breaks without calling rate_limits.wait_seconds, even when a skipped member resets inside WAIT_BUDGET_S (600 s). The requesty bench lifted after 472 s, so a wait would have reached a member with a 100% planner record (9/9 ok). A structural weakness adds to this: the 4-member planner list holds only 2 distinct models (nemotron-ultra twice, qwen3.8-27b twice). One provider-wide bad hour on either model therefore takes out half the list.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] When a pass ends with no success, wait for the soonest bench or cooldown reset whenever at least one member was skipped for a bench or cooldown and that reset falls inside the wait budget. Today the code waits only when every member was rate limited. Members that already timed out or errored in this call are excluded from later passes, so a stalled member is not re-hit at 120 s per pass. Log the wait as the existing ratewait row. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_failover_list (replace the `limited_only` break condition with a `has_pending_reset` check and track a per-call `failed_hard` set)) -> This run would have waited about 8 minutes and then called requesty nemotron-ultra (planner 9/9 ok) instead of failing. Any list with a mix of timeouts and near-term benches stops failing early.
- [model_per_role] Diversify the planner list so it has at least 3 distinct models, not 2 models on 2 providers each. Candidates with a measured clean record include nemotron-3-super-120b (94% over 52 calls). Present this to the captain with the ledger evidence first. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] planner) -> A single model's provider-wide outage or daily quota no longer removes half the planner list. [needs captain review]
- [prompt_context] Give the planner role its own stall timeout, sized from that member's measured p95 latency with a cap. Today every role shares one fixed 120 s. The 550B nemotron plans at a p50 of 55 s, so 120 s leaves little headroom on a large spec. As an alternative, put the fast qwen3.8-27b member (p50 1.8 s) first when it is available. (where: hive/models.py CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S use in _invoke_failover_list (_ChainMember timeout_s per tier)) -> Fewer planner timeouts on slow but healthy members, and less than 120 s lost per stall.
- [caching] Measure and remove the ~9-10 s spent per skipped hop. Read the chain_state snapshot once per pass instead of re-reading after a failed fetch, and confirm whether ledger.append or the snapshot reader is slow. (where: hive/chain_state.py ChainState.snapshot (failure TTL path) and hive/models.py _invoke_failover_list) -> Saves about 30-40 s of dead wall time per exhausted list and gives fresher bench data for the wait decision.
- [smaller_units] Before the planner node starts, preflight the planner list against chain_state. If every member is benched or cooling and the soonest reset is beyond the wait budget, requeue the run for that reset time instead of launching and failing. (where: hive/graphs/build_free.py launch path (preflight before the planner node)) -> Turns a guaranteed failed run into a scheduled one with no wasted 165 s run.

ready.title: hive: Chain waits for a bench reset even after a member stalls
ready.body:
In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, any non-rate-limit failure (a stall or an error) currently sets limited_only=False, and the loop then breaks. As a result the chain never waits for a benched or cooling member whose reset falls inside WAIT_BUDGET_S. Run pilot-11b7060b4962-1791445435 failed at 138 s this way. Kilo nemotron stalled, and requesty nemotron's bench ended about 280 s later, well inside the 600 s budget. Change: after a pass with no success, if soonest is set (at least one member was benched, cooling down, or newly rate limited), compute rate_limits.wait_seconds and wait, then retry the pass. This holds regardless of stalls or errors in that pass. Break only when soonest is None or the wait is 0. Stalled members already go to the end of the order through STALLS.order. Log the wait as the existing ratewait row. Regression tests in tests/: (1) Member A stalls and member B is benched until now+30 s. The test asserts one ratewait row, then B is called and returns ok. Use a fake clock and sleep. (2) Member A errors and no member has a reset. The test asserts the chain fails immediately with no ratewait row. (3) Member A stalls and B's reset is past the budget. The test asserts the chain fails with no wait. Run ./run-tests.sh to completion.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-11b7060b4962-1791445435 (task 11b7060b4962: 11b7060b4962).
Root cause: The planner's failover list was exhausted in about 138 s without a single successful call. Only one of its four members was actually called, and it stalled. The other three were skipped because they were already benched or cooling down. The list also holds only two models, each reached through two platforms, so one bad stretch for a model takes out half the list. Kilo's nemotron-3-ultra hit the 120 s stall timeout (CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S, ledger timeouts_s 120.8). That model's planner p50 is already 54.9 s. Cloudflare qwen3.8-27b was benched until 2026-10-09 00:00. Requesty nemotron-3-ultra was benched until 07:50:52Z, about 4.6 minutes after the failure. Groq qwen3.8-27b was rate limited until 08:15:27Z. In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, any non-rate-limit failure sets limited_only=False, and the loop then breaks instead of waiting. So the single stall stopped the chain from waiting for requesty's bench to end. That wait was about 4.6 minutes, well inside the 600 s WAIT_BUDGET_S, and requesty's nemotron is 9/9 ok as planner. The same state caused the identical failure of run pilot-11b7060b4962-1791445201 three minutes earlier, so the relaunch reran into an unchanged chain state.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] When a pass ends with no success, wait for the soonest reset if any member is benched or cooling down and that reset falls inside the wait budget and deadline. This applies even when another member stalled or errored. On the next pass, move the stalled member to the end of the list (STALLS.order already does this). Fail at once only when no member has a future reset. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (limited_only / break logic)) -> This run would have waited about 280 s and then called requesty nemotron-ultra, which is 9/9 ok as planner, instead of failing at 138 s. This removes the class of failure where a benched or cooling member could still have recovered within budget.
- [rate_limit_scheduling] At launch, read the chain_state bench table and rate_limits.COOLDOWNS for every member of each role list in the profile. If every member of a role is benched or cooling down past the wait budget, defer the run until the soonest reset, or refuse it with that reset time, instead of starting and failing in the planner. (where: hive/graphs/build_free.py launch path (or hive/profiles.py profile resolution)) -> Avoids back-to-back doomed runs like -1791445201 and -1791445435, which failed identically three minutes apart and each spent about 2 minutes of wall time.
- [model_per_role] Widen the free planner list from 2 distinct models to at least 4, drawn from measured history. Candidates are gemini-3.7-flash (7/7 ok, p50 4.3 s, used as reviewer but needs a non-billed route) and nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free (94% ok). distinct_roles must stay satisfied. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] planner) -> A single model's bench or stall no longer removes half the planner list. [needs captain review]
- [prompt_context] Give the planner member its own stall timeout, or send planner calls as streamed requests so the 120 s read timeout bounds silence rather than total generation time. The current nemotron-ultra planner p50 is 54.9 s, so a long plan can cross 120 s with no reply. (where: hive/models.py CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S / _ChainMember construction in _invoke_chain) -> Fewer false timeouts on slow but healthy planner members.
- [smaller_units] Split the spec into two tasks: an agent-pubkey deny-list with mention override, and a per-thread reply cap with human reset. Each gets its own test contract. (where: task spec 11b7060b4962 (planner input)) -> Shorter planner prompts and plans, so lower latency and fewer stall timeouts on the slow planner model.

ready.title: hive: Reviewer model outage retries review, not a worker fix round
ready.body:
In hive/nodes/reviewer.py, the `if not call_result.ok:` branch returns Review(verdict='fix') with no infra_failure flag. A rate-limited or timed-out reviewer therefore spends one of the task's 3 fix rounds and re-runs the worker on an unchanged diff. Run pilot-0c6eacb8f3c8-1791442588 lost a correct iter-1 commit this way: 9 reviewer calls hit 429 or a timeout, the unit was exhausted, and nothing merged. Change: when the deterministic gates and existing tests passed and the review model call fails, retry the call in place after the soonest cooldown reset (at most 2 retries, about 180 s total). If it still fails, return Review(verdict='fix', infra_failure=True, fix_brief=None, findings=['INFRA: review model unavailable']). In hive/graphs/build.py route_after_review, send an infra_failure review whose branch HEAD is unchanged back to the reviewer, not the worker, and block after INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT. Regression tests in tests/test_reviewer_model_outage.py: (1) with invoke_with_ledger stubbed to fail twice and then return a pass verdict, the review is 'pass' and the worker is never re-dispatched. (2) With it always failing, the Review has infra_failure=True and Review.exhausted() is False at iteration 3. (3) route_after_review on that Review routes to the reviewer node. Run ./run-tests.sh green before the PR.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-0c6eacb8f3c8-1791442588 (task 0c6eacb8f3c8: hive: Run shell-metachar acceptance tests through bash -c).
Root cause: The code was right, and the free reviewer models' rate limits turned it into a non-merge. Unit update-command-for committed a correct change on iter 1 (1f73b4f8), and its acceptance tests passed (rc=0). All 9 reviewer model calls for that unit then failed with a timeout or 429 on glm-4.5-flash, gemma-4-31b-it and glm-4.7-flash. In hive/nodes/reviewer.py, `if not call_result.ok:` turns a failed model call into Review(verdict="fix") with no infra_failure flag. Each reviewer outage therefore cost the unit a full worker round. Iters 2 and 3 re-ran the worker on an unchanged diff ("The change is already in place and verified"). Iter 3 hit a deterministic test failure (the acceptance run with bare `python` returned rc=1). That reached MAX_FIX_ITERATIONS=3, so Review.exhausted() blocked the unit. completed_task_ids() counts exhausted-blocked tasks as completed, so plan.ready() released the dependent unit add-regression-tests anyway. _base_branch_for() merges only PASSED dependency branches. With none, it fell back to base `main`, and the dependent worktree sits on 1cd7134a without the testing.py change. Its scope was only tests/test_testing_commands.py, so it could never pass. The worker returned BLOCKED ("hive/testing.py is not in this round's writable files") on 3 of 4 rounds, and the adjudicator twice answered side=module. That spent 38 more steps and 580k input tokens. Nothing merged, and the gate reported 0 files changed. The free chain was not the main cause. Worker calls were 92 of 115 ok, and the test_writer and planner calls were all ok.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] When the review model call fails (timeout, 429 or failover exhausted) after deterministic gates and existing tests passed, do not return a worker fix round. Retry the review call in place after the soonest cooldown reset, at most 2 retries within about 180 s. If it still fails, return Review(verdict='fix', infra_failure=True, fix_brief=None) and have route_after_review send that task back to the reviewer, not the worker, up to INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT. Then block with 'INFRA: review model unavailable'. (where: hive/nodes/reviewer.py review node, the `if not call_result.ok:` branch, plus hive/graphs/build.py route_after_review) -> This run's iter-1 commit would have been reviewed and passed. That saves 2 worker rounds (27 steps, about 400k input tokens), and the unit could not have been exhausted by reviewer outages.
- [smaller_units] Do not dispatch a task whose dependency ended blocked or exhausted. Mark it blocked at once with the finding 'dependency <id> did not pass', because _base_branch_for would hand it a base without the dependency's code. (where: hive/contracts.py Plan.ready() (or a passed-only variant used by the dispatch edge in hive/graphs/build.py) and the dispatch path that calls _base_branch_for) -> Removes the doomed add-regression-tests unit in runs like this one. That saves 38 worker steps and about 580k input tokens (41% of the run).
- [prompt_context] At plan validation, merge a task whose files_edit is a subset of a task it depends on, when that dependency already edits the same test file. Here, add-regression-tests duplicated update-command-for's test edits. (where: hive/contracts.py Plan validation (validate()), alongside the existing integration_order checks) -> One unit instead of two for a 3-line fix plus tests. That halves test_writer, worker and reviewer calls on small tasks.
- [model_per_role] Put nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free (reviewer history: 52 calls, 100% ok, 0% rate-limited) ahead of glm-4.5-flash, gemma-4-31b-it and glm-4.7-flash in the free profile's reviewer list. Those three produced every reviewer failure in this run (timeouts and 429s). (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] reviewer list) -> Fewer reviewer outages under load. Nemotron-ultra answered both of its successful reviewer calls in this run. [needs captain review]
- [caching] When a fix-round worker returns with written=[] and the branch HEAD is unchanged since the last review, reuse the previous deterministic gate and acceptance results keyed by (task_id, HEAD sha). Re-run only the review model call. (where: hive/nodes/reviewer.py deterministic_gates call site and hive/tool_loop.py acceptance run path) -> No repeat test runs on an identical diff. It also avoids a flaky re-run, like the iter-3 bare-python rc=1, flipping a green unit to red.
ready.name: hive reviewer model outage
ready.outcome: A reviewer 429 or timeout no longer burns a worker fix round. A green unit is re-reviewed and merges instead of being exhausted.

ready.title: hive: Failover chain waits on benches after a stall, not just 429s
ready.body:
Change: in hive/models.py::_invoke_chain, a single stalled member (rate_limits.is_stall) currently sets limited_only=False and breaks out of the loop. That skips the bench wait even when every other member is benched to a known, near time. Replace the break condition so the loop also waits and retries when every non-limited failure in the pass was a stall and `soonest` is set. Keep the existing WAIT_BUDGET_S and wait_until bounds. STALLS.order already moves the stalled member last for the next pass. Log the wait as the usual node='ratewait' row, with error text naming the stall. Regression test (write first, in tests/): fake a 4-member list. Member A is unbenched and its call returns 'Request timed out.'. Member B is benched by chain_state until now+30s. Members C and D are on cooldown for an hour. Stub rate_limits.sleep and the clock. Assert one ratewait row of about 30 s, then a call to B that succeeds and returns ok. Also assert that two stalls with no benched member still fail with 'failover list exhausted'. Run ./run-tests.sh.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-5cf5636064cc-1791445691 (task 5cf5636064cc: 5cf5636064cc).
Root cause: The planner's failover loop in hive/models.py::_invoke_chain gave up after 196 s. It had used 51 s of its 600 s rate-wait budget, and one member was about 48 s from coming off its bench. Pass 1 (07:48:21-27): all 4 planner members were benched or on cooldown. Kilo nemotron was benched to 07:49:20, Requesty nemotron to 07:49:21, Cloudflare qwen to 2026-10-09 and Groq qwen to 08:15:27. The loop correctly waited 51 s. Pass 2: Kilo nemotron was the only callable member and returned nothing for 120 s, which hit the CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S read timeout. By then the chain had re-benched Requesty nemotron only to 07:52:19. Because the Kilo failure was a timeout, `limited_only` became False. `if not limited_only: break` then ended the loop, and the bench wait never ran. The rule is that one stall disqualifies the wait-and-retry even when every other member is benched for a short, known time. A second cause sits in the list itself. The 4 planner rungs carry only 2 distinct models, and on this morning one gateway per model was out for hours (Cloudflare qwen till tomorrow, Groq qwen till 08:15). So the run depended on the slow nemotron (planner p50 54.9 s) answering within 120 s of silence. The earlier run, pilot-5cf5636064cc-1791445211 at 07:43Z, failed with the identical trail.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] In the failover loop, keep waiting after a stall when the pass called at most one member and every other member was skipped as benched or on cooldown. Wait for the soonest bench expiry within the rate-wait budget, rather than breaking. Concretely, compute `retryable = limited_only or (all non-limited failures are rate_limits.is_stall and soonest is not None)`, then break only when that is False. The stalled member is already moved last by STALLS.order, so the next pass tries the newly unbenched member first. (where: hive/models.py::_invoke_chain (the `if not limited_only: break` check after the member loop)) -> This run would have waited about 48 s and then called Requesty nemotron at 07:52:19 instead of failing. Planner exhaustion on mixed stall-plus-bench mornings turns into a bounded wait, capped by the existing 600 s budget.
- [model_per_role] Add a third distinct planner model so the list is not 2 models on 4 rungs. One candidate is a reviewer-proven model on a platform not already in the planner list, for example gemini-3.7-flash (100% ok, p50 4.3 s) through a free gateway, or glm-4.5-flash through zhipu. Also put qwen3.8-27b (p50 1.8 s) ahead of nemotron. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] planner) -> Losing one gateway per model no longer empties the planner list. A fast first rung also cuts typical planner latency from about 55 s to about 2 s. [needs captain review]
- [prompt_context] Give the planner role its own stall timeout, for example HIVE_CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S_PLAN defaulting to 180 s, or stream planner calls so the read timeout bounds silence rather than total generation. Nemotron-ultra's planner p50 is 54.9 s and its tail can exceed 120 s of silence on a non-streamed call. (where: hive/models.py::_invoke_chain (_ChainMember timeout_s) and the CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S definition) -> A slow but working planner model is not cut off as a timeout, which removes the failover:timeout hop that triggered this failure.
- [caching] When a pass called no members because every one was benched or cooling, compare the soonest expiry with the run deadline before the first wait. If no member comes back within the budget, fail fast with a 'planner list unavailable until <ts>' reason. That stops the pilot relaunching the same task every 8 minutes into the same benches. (where: hive/models.py::_invoke_chain and the pilot relaunch path that re-queued 5cf5636064cc at 07:43Z and 07:51Z) -> No more wasted back-to-back relaunches into an identical exhausted list. A clear retry-after time comes back for scheduling.
ready.name: hive failover chain waits
ready.outcome: A planner list with one stalled member and one member benched briefly waits for the bench and succeeds instead of exhausting.

ready.title: hive: test_writer: show dependency modules and interface in brief
ready.body:
Run pilot-f3d890fb845a-1791442111 shipped nothing because the test-only task's brief never showed hive/nodes/planner.py or the sibling task's interface validate_plan. public_surface matched only hive.target and hive.project_env, since \bplanner\b does not match inside test_node_planner. codestral invented validate_plan(dict).valid/.problems while the worker built validate_plan(plan, state) -> list[str].

Change in hive/nodes/test_writer.py:
(1) In test_writer(), extend the public_surface file list with the .py files_edit and files_create of every task in task.depends_on, read from the plan in the envelope. Pass the plan through _envelope in hive/graphs/build.py if it is not there yet.
(2) Map an edited tests/test_<x>.py or tests/test_node_<x>.py to an existing hive/<x>.py or hive/nodes/<x>.py and include it.
(3) In build_test_brief(), add a DEPENDENCY CONTRACT block listing each dependency's id, Interface and Goal.

Regression test first, in tests/test_test_writer_brief.py: build a Plan from this run's real planner-plan-1.json, stored as a fixture. Assert the brief for test-interface-validation contains 'module hive.nodes.planner' and 'validate_plan'. Assert a task with no depends_on gets an unchanged brief.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-f3d890fb845a-1791442111 (task f3d890fb845a: hive: planner repairs an edit task whose interface symbol is missing).
Root cause: Two independent failures stacked, and either one alone would have stopped the merge. (1) The test contract could never pass. The planner split the work into an implementation task (interface "validate_plan") and a test-only task that depends on it (interface: the two test names only). test_writer.build_test_brief built PUBLIC SURFACE from public_surface(files_edit, goal+interface). The test task edits only tests/test_node_planner.py, and "\bplanner\b" does not match inside "test_node_planner", so hive/nodes/planner.py was never shown. Only hive.target and hive.project_env appeared, and the brief named "validate_plan" zero times. codestral therefore invented validate_plan(plan_dict) returning an object with .valid and .problems. The worker independently wrote validate_plan(plan, state) returning list[str]. The test task's worktree also lacked the implementation, so every check died with ImportError (rc=2). (2) The implementation task was never approved. Its only reviewer call exhausted the whole review list: glm-4.5-flash timed out after 121 s, gemma-4-31b was on a cooldown that reset within about 2 minutes, glm-4.7-flash was benched for about 1 minute, and the rest were benched until the next day. The reviewer node failed outright instead of waiting the ~100 s for the soonest reset. With no approved task, the integrator merged 0 files.
Optimizations:
- [prompt_context] When a task depends on other tasks in the plan, add their files_edit/files_create .py modules to the public_surface file list. Also add a 'DEPENDENCY CONTRACT' block giving each dependency's id, Interface and Goal. Also map tests/test_<x>.py and tests/test_node_<x>.py edits to their existing source module (hive/nodes/<x>.py, hive/<x>.py). (where: hive/nodes/test_writer.py test_writer() (surface computation) and build_test_brief() (new dependency block). The plan reaches it through hive/graphs/build.py _envelope) -> A test-only task's brief shows the real module under test and the dependency's interface. This removes the invented-signature class that made test-interface-validation unpassable on every iteration
- [rate_limit_scheduling] When the reviewer's failover list is exhausted and the soonest member cooldown or bench reset is under 5 minutes, sleep until that reset and retry once. Write a ratewait ledger row the way the worker path does, instead of marking the review failed. (where: hive/nodes/reviewer.py, the review model invocation (the invoke_with_ledger call site)) -> The add-interface-validation review would have waited about 100 s for gemma-4-31b and run. Transient chain exhaustion stops discarding finished work
- [smaller_units] Reject or merge a plan task whose files_edit are only test files and whose depends_on task carries the code under test. Fold such tests into the implementation task's acceptance_tests so test and code share one worktree and one contract. (where: hive/nodes/planner.py grounding_problems() or Plan.repair()) -> The test task no longer runs in a worktree without the implementation, which removes the ImportError loop that burned 33 worker steps
- [other] Drop files_create entries that are fragments of an acceptance command, such as a token containing quotes or parentheses or not path-shaped. (where: hive/nodes/planner.py Plan.repair() / ground_plan()) -> Stops garbage paths like importable')" from turning an edit task into a create task, which would also bypass the interface-symbol check this task adds
- [model_per_role] Move gemma-4-31b-it ahead of glm-4.5-flash in the free profile reviewer list. Both show 100% ok in history, but glm-4.5-flash timed out at 121 s here. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] reviewer list) -> Fewer reviewer timeouts burning two minutes before the first failover [needs captain review]
ready.name: hive test writer show
ready.outcome: A test-only task's brief names the dependency's interface and shows its module, so the tests target the real signature.

ready.title: hive: Failover chain waits for a short bench even after a stall
ready.body:
Change hive/models.py _invoke_chain. Today any non-rate-limit failure (stall, timeout, 5xx) in a pass sets limited_only=False, and the chain breaks without waiting. That happens even when another member's chain bench or cooldown ends within seconds. Run pilot-11b7060b4962-1791445926 failed this way: requesty nemotron-ultra stalled 120 s, and kilo nemotron-ultra's bench ended 64 s later, at 07:55:29. Change the gate so that after a pass with no success, the chain computes the soonest reset among members that were skipped as benched or cooldown. If rate_limits.wait_seconds(soonest, now, spent, deadline_left) > 0, it writes the ratewait row, sleeps, and runs another pass. On the retry pass, members that stalled or errored in the previous pass stay last (STALLS.order) and are tried at most once more. Total waiting stays bounded by WAIT_BUDGET_S and wait_until. The exhausted error message and failover rows are unchanged. Regression test, written first from this spec, in tests/test_models_failover.py (or the existing failover test module): a 3-member list where member A is benched until now+30 s, member B returns 'Request timed out.', and member C is on cooldown until now+3600 s. Fake the clock and sleep. Assert one ratewait row with about 30 s, then a second pass that calls A and returns its ok result. Add a second case where the only bench ends after WAIT_BUDGET_S and assert the call fails without waiting. Run ./run-tests.sh green.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-11b7060b4962-1791445926 (task 11b7060b4962: 11b7060b4962).
Root cause: The planner's 4-member free list was effectively one model, and the chain gave up instead of waiting for it. The cloudflare qwen3.8 member was benched by the chain until 2026-10-09 and the groq qwen3.8 member was rate limited until 08:15:27. That left only nemotron-3-ultra on two platforms, kilo and requesty. About six concurrent pilot runs were hitting that model as planner and reviewer, and the ledger shows repeated 502s, 429s and stalls on it from 07:15 onward. In this run the requesty call went silent for the full 120 s CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S and failed with "Request timed out." In hive/models.py, _invoke_chain then set limited_only=False, which hits `if not limited_only: break`. So the chain skipped the rate-wait path, even though kilo's bench expired at 07:55:29, about 64 s after the 07:54:25 failure and well inside the 600 s WAIT_BUDGET_S. A single stall disqualifies the wait, and the run fails at once. The same task was also relaunched 3 times in 12 minutes, and each attempt failed the same way and burned about 2 minutes. This is a scheduling and failover-policy failure, not a model-quality one. The planner never produced a single token (tokens_in 0, tokens_out 0).
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] After a pass with no success, wait for the soonest bench or cooldown reset, then retry. Do this whenever some member's reset falls inside the wait budget and deadline, even if another member stalled or errored in that pass. Retry only the members that were benched or cooled down, not the one that just stalled. Log the wait as a ratewait row as now. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (the `if not limited_only: break` gate), using rate_limits.wait_seconds) -> This run would have waited about 64 s and then called kilo nemotron-ultra, which was then free, instead of failing. It turns stall-plus-short-bench failures, 3 of the 3 runs on this task, into retries within the existing 600 s budget.
- [model_per_role] Add a third distinct model family to the planner list, so it is not two routes of nemotron-ultra plus two routes of qwen3.8. Candidate from measured history: nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free (94.2% ok, p50 4.6 s, 52 calls). Respect distinct_roles, because it currently sits in no free role list. (where: hive/policy.toml [profiles.free] planner) -> When qwen3.8 is benched for the day and nemotron-ultra is saturated, the planner still has an independent live member. That removes the single-model collapse seen at 07:15 to 07:54. [needs captain review]
- [rate_limit_scheduling] Before launching or relaunching a build-free run, check chain_state.STATE.benched_until and rate_limits.COOLDOWNS for every planner member. If none is callable for more than about 60 s, defer the launch to the soonest reset instead of starting a run that fails in about 2 minutes. Also cap concurrent planner calls per member, for example 1 in flight per free member, so parallel pilots queue instead of stalling one route. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (per-member in-flight semaphore), plus the pilot or run-task launch path that relaunched 11b7060b4962 3 times in 12 minutes) -> This stops repeated doomed relaunches (3 x 135 s wasted here) and reduces the 502 and 429 storm on nemotron-ultra caused by about 6 concurrent runs.
- [caching] Persist a successful planner output keyed by task id and spec hash. A relaunch of the same task then reuses the plan instead of calling the planner again. (where: hive/nodes/planner.py planner node (read cache before invoking, write after ok)) -> Relaunches after a later-stage failure skip the most contended role entirely and cut planner load from reruns to zero.
- [prompt_context] Trim the planner prompt (successful nemotron-ultra planner calls take 6 to 8.6k tokens in, p50 54.9 s) by capping injected repo or atlas context. Make the stall timeout per role, so a slow-but-alive planner gets more than 120 s of silence before handover, or stream so a first token arrives earlier. (where: hive/nodes/planner.py prompt assembly; hive/models.py CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S becomes per-node) -> Fewer stall timeouts on a large model under load. Tokens out arrive sooner, so the 120 s read timeout trips less often.
ready.name: hive failover chain waits
ready.outcome: A failover list with a stalled member and another member benched under the wait budget waits and retries instead of failing.

ready.title: hive: planner: reject plan interfaces naming nonexistent symbols
ready.body:
Run pilot-fcfe779c2e88-1791442508 spent 3 worker rounds (all stop_reason=deadline, zero edits to hive/nodes/reviewer.py in rounds 2-3) searching for 'review_node' and 'determine_verdict'. The planner invented those names in task.interface. The real function is reviewer() at reviewer.py:1586.

Change: add interface_symbol_problems(plan, root) in hive/nodes/planner.py. For each task, take identifier tokens from task.interface and check each one against the top-level def/class/assignment names of every files_edit file, read from the mirror checkout via tool_loop.file_outline. Skip names that are created by files_create. Each missing name yields a problem of the form "<task>: interface names <sym> but none of <files_edit> defines it (defined: a, b, c ...)" with up to 15 real names. Call it from _planner next to grounding_problems() so the existing retry path replans. If root is unavailable, return []. The function must never raise.

Regression test (tests/test_planner_interface_symbols.py, written first): (1) tmp repo with pkg/mod.py defining def reviewer and def deterministic_gates. A plan with files_edit ['pkg/mod.py'] and interface 'review_node, determine_verdict' yields 2 problems naming both symbols and listing 'reviewer'. (2) interface 'reviewer' yields []. (3) A symbol defined in the task's files_create is not flagged. (4) A missing root yields [].

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-fcfe779c2e88-1791442508 (task fcfe779c2e88: hive: an ORPHAN finding ends the run with no fix round).
Root cause: The run had two subtasks, and neither landed the fix. The implementation subtask (reviewer-orphan-fix-logic, files_edit hive/nodes/reviewer.py + tests/test_node_reviewer.py) used all 3 fix rounds without one edit to hive/nodes/reviewer.py. Every round ended with stop_reason "deadline" after 11 to 18 steps, and rounds 2 and 3 were 100% read_file/search calls. The worker spent those rounds hunting for symbols that do not exist. The planner's interface string "review_node, determine_verdict" was invented, and the planner's Atlas grounding for reviewer.py was stale (atlas_state "no_symbol", function `reviewer` listed at lines 1108/1090/1057/... with Windows paths, while the real def is at line 1586). Each round searched "def review_node|def determine_verdict" again and re-paged the same 2,000-line ranges (1121-1260, 1586-2039, 420-600). The "already read last round" summary carries only range names, not content, so it saved nothing. A second cause wasted round 1: the test-first contract from codestral could not compile against hive's API. It imported nonexistent modules (hive.worktree, hive.task, hive.worker_result), passed WorkerResult(findings=...), called apply_hard_item_gate with 9 positional args against a 7-parameter signature, and passed its tuple to parse_verdict(text). So round 1's only writes were repairs to that test file. The second subtask (test-reviewer-orphan-new-file) had test-only scope. Its worker found the right edit but its two edit_file calls on hive/nodes/reviewer.py were refused (ok=False), so it committed a test alone. Nothing changed in the shipped code, and the gate reported "0 files changed".
Optimizations:
- [prompt_context] Add interface_symbol_problems(plan, root): for each task, split task.interface into identifiers and require each to appear as a `def <name>`/`class <name>`/top-level assignment in one of the task's files_edit files, read from the run's mirror checkout. Unknown names become planner problems that trigger the existing retry, listing the real top-level symbols of each files_edit file so the replan names actual anchors (for example reviewer, deterministic_gates, apply_hard_item_gate). (where: hive/nodes/planner.py: new interface_symbol_problems(), called from _planner next to grounding_problems()) -> Workers stop spending whole rounds searching for invented functions. In this run that removes the repeated review_node/determine_verdict searches and points the worker at reviewer.py:1586 and the ORPHAN block at 494-500 in round 1.
- [caching] Verify Atlas grounding against the real file before it reaches the worker. When outline line numbers or symbol names do not match the mirror checkout (as with this run's stale reviewer@1108 entries with Windows paths), replace them with a local file_outline() of the checkout and mark atlas_state 'stale'. (where: hive/nodes/planner.py: ground_with_atlas()) -> The worker gets correct line anchors for a 2,000-line file, so it reads fewer ranges before its first edit.
- [smaller_units] Validate the test-first file before dispatch. Run pytest --collect-only on it in the worktree, and on ImportError/NameError/TypeError at collection, regenerate it once with the collection error and the real signatures of the imported symbols in the prompt. Never hand an uncollectable contract to the worker. (where: hive/nodes/test_writer.py: after the test file is written, before the worker envelope is built) -> Saves the worker round spent repairing codestral's bad imports and signatures. Round 1 goes to the implementation.
- [smaller_units] Add a planner problem when a task's goal or interface names a fix in a file that only a different task may edit, and that task has no depends_on edge to it (here, the test task tried to implement the fix in reviewer.py and was refused). Require the regression test to share the implementation task, or to depend on it. (where: hive/nodes/planner.py: grounding_problems() or a new scope_split_problems()) -> Removes the refused edit_file calls and the orphan test-only commit that cannot pass without the implementation.
- [prompt_context] On a fix round, carry the actual text of the 1-2 most-read line ranges of each files_edit file from the previous round, capped at about 150 lines, alongside the existing 'already read last round' range list. Today only the range names travel. (where: hive/graphs/build.py: _envelope() and hive/nodes/tool_worker.py: _read_set_summary()) -> Rounds 2 and 3 start at the edit instead of re-paging 1586-2039 and 420-600, so the edit lands inside the deadline.
ready.name: hive planner reject plan
ready.outcome: A plan whose interface names a function absent from its files_edit is replanned, so workers start from real symbols.

ready.title: hive: Failover waits for cooldown reset after mixed timeout pass
ready.body:
In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, a pass currently breaks as soon as any member times out (limited_only=False), even when another member's cooldown resets within the wait budget. Run pilot-5cf5636064cc-1791446407 failed this way. Its planner retry hit 2 nemotron timeouts and groq qwen3.8-27b on a 9-minute cooldown, and ratewait_s was 0.

Change: track members that failed on a 429/cooldown/bench separately from those that timed out or errored. When the pass ends with no success and soonest is set and rate_limits.wait_seconds(...) > 0, log the normal ratewait row, sleep, and retry only the rate-limited members. Members that timed out or errored in this call are not re-called. Keep the existing wait budget and wait_until deadline. A pass whose failures are all timeouts or errors still fails immediately. Surgical change only. Do not alter existing behaviour for all-limited or all-timeout passes.

Regression tests in tests/test_models_failover.py (or the existing _invoke_chain test file):
(1) member A times out and member B is on cooldown resetting in 5 s (fake clock and sleep). The call returns B's OK result, writes exactly one ratewait row, and calls A once.
(2) all members time out. There is no ratewait row and the call fails as today.
(3) A times out and B's cooldown exceeds the remaining budget. The call fails without sleeping.
Run ./run-tests.sh fully green.

---
From the Opus analysis of failed build-free run pilot-5cf5636064cc-1791446407 (task 5cf5636064cc: 5cf5636064cc).
Root cause: The first planner call succeeded (nemotron-3-ultra via kilo, 142.8 s, 4852 tokens out), but its plan failed validation. That sent the planner into validation retry 1 (hive/nodes/planner.py _planner, the `while problems and attempt <= PLAN_RETRIES` loop) with a longer prompt carrying the retry_reason. On that retry the 4-member planner list held only one usable model. free:cloudflare:@cf/qwen/qwen3.8-27b was benched by the chain until 2026-10-09T00:00Z. free:groq:qwen/qwen3.8-27b was rate limited until 08:15:27Z, about 9 minutes away. The two remaining routes were the same model, nemotron-3-ultra on kilo and on requesty, and each went silent past CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S=120 s: 241.2 s of timeouts is about 2 x 120.6 s. In hive/models.py _invoke_chain, any timeout sets limited_only=False, so the pass ends with `if not limited_only: break` and the call fails. It never waits roughly 9 minutes for groq qwen3.8-27b, which has 7 of 7 planner calls OK at a 1.8 s p50. Two earlier runs of this task (07:43Z, 07:51Z) failed with the same shape. The plan's validation problems cannot be identified because no raw model-call files were kept.
Optimizations:
- [rate_limit_scheduling] When a failover pass ends with no success and at least one member on a cooldown or bench that resets within the remaining wait budget, wait for the soonest reset and retry only the members that were rate limited. Members that timed out or stalled in this call are not retried. Today any timeout sets limited_only=False and breaks immediately. (where: hive/models.py _invoke_chain (limited_only / soonest loop)) -> This run would have waited about 9 minutes for groq qwen3.8-27b (100% planner OK, 1.8 s p50) instead of failing. It turns the mixed timeout-plus-cooldown planner exhaustions seen in all 3 runs of this task into a landed plan.
- [smaller_units] Make a planner validation retry that fails on transport keep the last parsed plan. If the only remaining problems are mechanically repairable or are preference-level, proceed with it. Otherwise raise a ContractError that names the problems, not a bare ModelError. Persist the first raw planner reply and its problem list to the ledger so the failing validation is diagnosable. (where: hive/nodes/planner.py _planner (validation-retry while loop)) -> A good-enough first plan stops being discarded by a flaky retry. Every failed plan validation leaves the problem list on disk, which was missing for this run.
- [prompt_context] Give the plan role its own stall timeout, for example HIVE_CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_PLAN_S defaulting to 240 s. Reasoning planners stream no content while thinking, and the retry prompt is larger than the 4174-token first prompt that already took 142.8 s. (where: hive/models.py CHAIN_STALL_TIMEOUT_S and the _ChainMember construction in _invoke_chain (per-tier timeout)) -> nemotron-3-ultra retries stop being cut off at 120 s of thinking silence. That removes 2 of the 3 timeouts in this run.
- [model_per_role] Reorder the free planner list to put free:groq:qwen/qwen3.8-27b first. It has 100% OK at a 1.8 s p50 versus 54.9 s for nemotron-3-ultra.
